title: Underreaction, Salience, and Hot-Hand Beliefs in Sports Event-Contract Markets: Evidence from Kalshi NBA and NFL
items.abstract: <jats:p>Prediction markets are widely regarded as efficient aggregators of public information, yet how quickly their prices absorb that information, and whether the speed depends on how the information arrives, remains unsettled. In-play sports contracts let us examine this directly. Evolving game states yield an objective, second-by-second win-probability benchmark against which prices can be tracked trade by trade. We exploit this setting using 41.8 million transactions across 1,496 NBA and NFL games on Kalshi, matched to play-by-play benchmarks. In both sports, prices adjust to scoring news only gradually and incompletely within short post-event windows, a robust underreaction consistent with limited attention. The adjustment path tracks each sport&apos;s scoring structure. NBA prices drift steadily toward the benchmark after frequent, small shocks, whereas NFL prices settle at a flatter, less complete level after rarer, larger shocks. Salient, highlight-like events draw a weaker short-run response, most clearly in the NBA. Prices show no tendency to extrapolate scoring runs beyond fundamentals, leaving no role for hot-hand pricing. Although benchmark deviations exceed plausible fee-and-spread hurdles across the price distribution, a mean-reversion rule earns nothing net of costs. The market is inefficient in how fast it incorporates information, not in offering exploitable profit.</jats:p>

Bounded Event-Time Execution Architecture
items.abstract:
<jats:p>Contemporary cyber-physical and system-of-systems environments maintain sensing, synchronisation, coordination, and distributed processing capabilities across heterogeneous operational domains. Existing representational architectures define mechanisms for observation, modelling, and state coordination; however, operational state resolution remains externalised, deferred, or distributed across independent systems. Therefore, state formation proceeds through reconciliation, eventual consistency, or retrospective reconstruction rather than through bounded event-time execution. Bounded operational state-resolution semantics are not maintained within the execution domain itself.
This paper defines a bounded event-time execution architecture and an integrated Concept of Operations (CONOPS) in which admissible actions resolve into operational system state within bounded domains. The architecture is defined at both functional and operational levels.
Internal implementation constructs, deployment-specific mechanisms, and parameterisation remain abstracted from the architectural definition. Representational Digital Twin systems constitute one operational context but do not define the architectural scope of the contribution.
The architecture defines bounded event-time execution semantics and operational state-resolution behaviour for cyber-physical and system-of-systems environments. The architecture is defined as a specification-stage operational execution architecture intended to support subsequent implementation, deployment, and empirical evaluation.</jats:p>

Motivation and Psychological Contract in Sport Event Volunteerism: The Impact of Contract Fulfilment On Satisfaction and Future Behavioral Intention
items.abstract:
<jats:p>This study investigated sport event volunteer motivation and psychological contract (PC) with regard to the relationship between PC fulfilment, satisfaction, and future behavioral intention. Motivation-based volunteer subgroups based on cluster analysis were compared regarding their
 expectations and experiences of PC types as well as their overall satisfaction and future behavioral intention in a pre- and posttest study. The gap between expectations and experiences of PC types (PC fulfilment by gap: PCFg), and second, experience (satisfaction) of PC types (PC fulfilment
 by experience: PCFe) were tested using regression analysis to investigate the impact of PC fulfilment on satisfaction and future behavioral intention. The analysis was conducted on a sample of 261 sport event volunteers from three sport events in southeast Queensland, Australia. Among this
 volunteer sample, ideological PC was considered as the most important PC type overall, but different motivations were associated with different PC preferences. Volunteers who had different motivations had varying experiences of PC types, overall satisfaction, and intention to continue volunteering.
 PCFe was highly related to overall satisfaction and future behavioral intention and was found to be a better predictor of volunteer satisfaction than PCFg. This study provides important theoretical and practical implications for sport event volunteerism approached from the perspective of PC
 types and motivations.</jats:p>

title: Default-No: Contract-Gated Execution as Structural Governance for Autonomous AI Agents
items.abstract: <jats:p>Autonomous AI agents are being deployed in domains where their decisions carry legal, financial, and operational consequences. Every major deployment framework for these agents shares a structural deficiency: the system operates on a default-yes permission model. The agent decides, then acts, then logs. Guardrails intercept after the decision has been made. Audit trails reside in storage systems that the executing agent or its operators can modify. Knowledge access is filtered from results after the model has processed unauthorized content. When the system that produces a decision also controls the record of how that decision was made, trust is architecturally impossible regardless of the sophistication of the constraints applied. This paper presents contract-gated execution, a deterministic governance architecture in which no tool, API call, or external interaction can execute until all preconditions are independently verified against live system state. The architecture implements a default-no permission model: non-execution is the default state, and authorization must be explicitly constructed, registered, and satisfied at execution time against state managers that the execution engine cannot influence. Governance rules are implemented as frozen data structures that the runtime physically prevents from modification. Knowledge access operates through pre-restriction rather than postfiltering, ensuring that information outside an agent's authorized scope is never returned by the database, not merely hidden from the response. Audit records are written to append-only stores architecturally separated from execution authority. We present evidence from a production system operating 12,780 tools under contract governance across 10 autonomous agents organized into 3 organizational boards, with 352 venture profiles activated through the contract-gated pipeline. Promotion from staging to active status requires 100 or more executions, a 95% success rate, and 99% contract satisfaction. We argue that deterministic governance around probabilistic models is not a contradiction but an architectural necessity: the model suggests, the contract decides. This pattern is domain-agnostic and provides a structural foundation for compliance with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the EU AI Act, and IEEE P2863.</jats:p>

title: Contract-Gated Execution: A Deterministic Governance Layer for Autonomous AI Agent Orchestration
items.abstract: <jats:p>This submission responds to the OECD's call for implementation tools that enable trustworthy AI deployment in consequential domains. Contract-gated execution was developed as commercial infrastructure and is presented here as a governance pattern directly applicable to public-sector AI deployment. Government procurement officers, compliance auditors, regulatory reviewers, and public administrators are the intended adopters of this framework-any agency deploying autonomous AI agents in consequential decision-making would benefit from the deterministic governance properties described below. The pattern addresses a specific gap in current AI governance approaches: the absence of architecturally enforced constraints on autonomous AI agent behavior. Policy-based governance depends on enforcement mechanisms that may themselves be subject to override. Contract-gated execution makes unauthorized actions structurally impossible, not merely prohibited.</jats:p>
